entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.acceleration_eq_of_equationOfMotion
entries.docstring:
Solving the equation of motion for the acceleration: along a solution the second derivative
is `-(k/m) x - (γ/m) ẋ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma acceleration_eq_of_equationOfMotion (z : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hEOM : S.EquationOfMotion z) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ z) t = (-(S.m⁻¹ * S.k)) • z t + (-(S.m⁻¹ * S.γ)) • ∂ₜ z t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.isUnderdamped_or_isCriticallyDamped_or_isOverdamped
entries.docstring: Every damped oscillator is underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped.
entries.snippet:
lemma isUnderdamped_or_isCriticallyDamped_or_isOverdamped :
    S.IsUnderdamped ∨ S.IsCriticallyDamped ∨ S.IsOverdamped

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.lagrangian
entries.docstring:
The Caldirola–Kanai lagrangian of the damped harmonic oscillator. It is the
lagrangian of the underlying undamped harmonic oscillator multiplied by the
time-dependent factor `exp (γ/m * t)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def lagrangian (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.lagrangian_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq : S.lagrangian = fun (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) =>
    exp (S.γ / S.m * t) * (1 / (2 : ℝ) * S.m * ⟪v, v⟫_ℝ - 1 / (2 : ℝ) * S.k * ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.lagrangian_eq_exp_mul_kineticEnergy_sub_potentialEnergy
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_eq_exp_mul_kineticEnergy_sub_potentialEnergy (t : Time)
    (xₜ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.lagrangian t (xₜ t) (∂ₜ xₜ t) =
      exp (S.γ / S.m * t) * (S.kineticEnergy xₜ t - S.potentialEnergy (xₜ t))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.lagrangian_of_isUndamped
entries.docstring:
When the damping coefficient is zero, the Caldirola–Kanai lagrangian is the
lagrangian of the underlying undamped harmonic oscillator.
entries.snippet:
lemma lagrangian_of_isUndamped (hS : S.IsUndamped) :
    S.lagrangian = S.toHarmonicOscillator.lagrangian

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.contDiff_lagrangian
entries.snippet:
@[fun_prop]
lemma contDiff_lagrangian (n : WithTop ℕ∞) : ContDiff ℝ n ↿S.lagrangian

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradient_const_mul
ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradient_lagrangian_position_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_lagrangian_position_eq (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (fun x => S.lagrangian t x v) x = -(exp (S.γ / S.m * t) * S.k) • x

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradient_lagrangian_velocity_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma gradient_lagrangian_velocity_eq (t : Time) (x v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    gradient (S.lagrangian t x) v = (exp (S.γ / S.m * t) * S.m) • v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradLagrangian
entries.docstring: The variational gradient of the action of the damped harmonic oscillator.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def gradLagrangian (xₜ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradLagrangian_eq_eulerLagrangeOp
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_eq_eulerLagrangeOp (xₜ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ xₜ) :
    S.gradLagrangian xₜ = eulerLagrangeOp S.lagrangian xₜ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.deriv_exp_smul
entries.snippet:
private lemma deriv_exp_smul (a : ℝ) (y : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hy : Differentiable ℝ y) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t' : Time => exp (a * t'.val) • y t') t =
      exp (a * t.val) • (∂ₜ y t + a • y t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.gradLagrangian_eq_force
entries.docstring:
The variational gradient of the Caldirola–Kanai action is the exponential factor
times the difference of the force and mass times acceleration appearing in
Newton's second law.
entries.snippet:
lemma gradLagrangian_eq_force (xₜ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (hx : ContDiff ℝ ∞ xₜ) :
    S.gradLagrangian xₜ = fun t : Time =>
      exp (S.γ / S.m * t) • (force S xₜ t - S.m • ∂ₜ (∂ₜ xₜ) t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.equationOfMotion_iff_gradLagrangian_zero
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_iff_gradLagrangian_zero (xₜ : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hx : ContDiff ℝ ∞ xₜ) :
    S.EquationOfMotion xₜ ↔ S.gradLagrangian xₜ = 0

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectory_contDiff
entries.docstring: The selected trajectory is smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_contDiff (IC : InitialConditions) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (S.trajectory IC)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectory_apply_zero
entries.docstring: The selected trajectory has initial position `IC.x₀`.
entries.snippet: lemma trajectory_apply_zero (IC : InitialConditions) : S.trajectory IC 0 = IC.x₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectory_velocity_at_zero
entries.docstring: The selected trajectory has initial velocity `IC.v₀`.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectory_velocity_at_zero (IC : InitialConditions) :
    ∂ₜ (S.trajectory IC) 0 = IC.v₀

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.phaseVectorField
entries.docstring:
The phase-space vector field of the damped oscillator, sending `(x, ẋ)` to
`(ẋ, -(k/m) x - (γ/m) ẋ)`, as a continuous linear map on `E × E`.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.phaseVectorField_apply
entries.snippet:
private lemma phaseVectorField_apply (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) :
    S.phaseVectorField (a, b) = (b, (-(S.m⁻¹ * S.k)) • a + (-(S.m⁻¹ * S.γ)) • b)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.toRealCLE_symm_one
entries.snippet: private lemma toRealCLE_symm_one : Time.toRealCLE.symm (1 : ℝ) = (1 : Time)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm
entries.docstring:
Bridge from the time derivative to `HasDerivAt` for a curve reparametrised through the
canonical `ℝ ≃L[ℝ] Time` equivalence.
entries.snippet:
private lemma hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm (w : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (τ : ℝ)
    (hw : DifferentiableAt ℝ w (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => w (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ))
      (∂ₜ w (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ)) τ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.phaseCurve_hasDerivAt
entries.docstring:
The phase curve `τ ↦ (z t, ẋ t)` (with `t = toRealCLE.symm τ`) of a smooth solution `z`
solves the first-order phase-space ODE with vector field `phaseVectorField`.
entries.snippet:
private lemma phaseCurve_hasDerivAt (z : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hz : ContDiff ℝ ∞ z) (hEOM : S.EquationOfMotion z) (τ : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => (z (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ), ∂ₜ z (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ)))
      (S.phaseVectorField (z (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ), ∂ₜ z (Time.toRealCLE.symm τ))) τ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.equationOfMotion_unique
entries.docstring:
Any two smooth solutions of the damped equation of motion with the same initial position and
velocity are equal.
entries.snippet:
lemma equationOfMotion_unique (x y : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hx : ContDiff ℝ ∞ x) (hy : ContDiff ℝ ∞ y)
    (hEOMx : S.EquationOfMotion x) (hEOMy : S.EquationOfMotion y)
    (h0 : x 0 = y 0) (hv0 : ∂ₜ x 0 = ∂ₜ y 0) :
    x = y

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.DampedHarmonicOscillator.trajectories_unique
entries.docstring:
The selected trajectory is the unique smooth solution of the damped equation of motion with the
given initial conditions.
entries.snippet:
lemma trajectories_unique (IC : InitialConditions) (x : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
    (hx : ContDiff ℝ ∞ x) (hEOM : S.EquationOfMotion x)
    (hx0 : x 0 = IC.x₀) (hv0 : ∂ₜ x 0 = IC.v₀) :
    x = S.trajectory IC

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ConfigurationSpace.valDiffeomorph
entries.docstring:
The global coordinate chart as an analytic diffeomorphism between `ConfigurationSpace` and
its `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)` model, upgrading `valHomeomorphism` to a smooth identification.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.instNormedAddCommGroupTangent
entries.docstring: The model-space normed additive group structure on tangent spaces.
entries.snippet:
instance instNormedAddCommGroupTangent (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    NormedAddCommGroup (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.instNormedSpaceTangent
entries.docstring: The model-space real normed vector space structure on tangent spaces.
entries.snippet:
instance instNormedSpaceTangent (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    NormedSpace ℝ (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.tangentCoord
entries.docstring:
The chart-induced continuous linear equivalence from the tangent space at `q` to the
Euclidean coordinate model `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)`.
entries.snippet:
def tangentCoord (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.instFiniteDimensionalTangent
entries.docstring:
Each tangent space is finite-dimensional because it is linearly equivalent to
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)` through `tangentCoord`.
entries.snippet:
instance instFiniteDimensionalTangent (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    FiniteDimensional ℝ (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace
entries.docstring: The position in one-dimensional space associated to the configuration.
entries.snippet: def toSpace (q : ConfigurationSpace) : Space 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.ConfigurationSpace.toSpace_apply
entries.docstring:
The physical-space coordinate associated to a configuration is its chosen global
coordinate.
entries.snippet: lemma toSpace_apply (q : ConfigurationSpace) (i : Fin 1) : q.toSpace i = q.val i

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massMetricVal
entries.docstring:
The value of the oscillator mass metric at `q`. It is the mass-scaled pullback of the
Euclidean inner product along `tangentCoord q`, so
`massMetricVal S q v w = S.m * ⟪tangentCoord q v, tangentCoord q w⟫_ℝ`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def massMetricVal (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q →L[ℝ]
      TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q →L[ℝ] ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massMetricVal_apply
entries.docstring:
Applying the mass metric value to two tangent vectors gives the mass-scaled Euclidean
inner product of their coordinate representatives.
entries.snippet:
lemma massMetricVal_apply
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v w : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) :
    massMetricVal S q v w = S.m * ⟪tangentCoord q v, tangentCoord q w⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.tangentCoord_ne_zero
entries.docstring: A nonzero tangent vector has nonzero coordinate representative under `tangentCoord`.

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massMetricVal_pos
entries.docstring: The oscillator mass metric is positive on nonzero tangent vectors.
entries.snippet:
lemma massMetricVal_pos
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    0 < massMetricVal S q v v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massMetricVal_isVonNBounded
entries.docstring: The mass metric unit ball is bounded in the model norm.
entries.snippet:
lemma massMetricVal_isVonNBounded
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace) :
    IsVonNBounded ℝ
      {v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q | massMetricVal S q v v < 1}

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massMetricVal_contMDiff
entries.docstring: The oscillator mass metric is constant in the global tangent-bundle chart.
entries.snippet:
lemma massMetricVal_contMDiff (S : HarmonicOscillator) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
      (𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)).prod
        𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) →L[ℝ]
          EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ)) ω
      (fun q : ConfigurationSpace =>
        TotalSpace.mk'
          (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ)
          (E := fun q : ConfigurationSpace =>
            TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q →L[ℝ]
              TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q →L[ℝ] ℝ)
          q (massMetricVal S q))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massRiemannianMetric
entries.docstring:
The mass-scaled Euclidean inner product as a Riemannian metric on the oscillator
configuration space.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def massRiemannianMetric (S : HarmonicOscillator) :
    ContMDiffRiemannianMetric 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) ω
      (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))
      (TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) : ConfigurationSpace → Type _) where

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.geometricKineticEnergy
entries.docstring: The defining formula for the oscillator geometric kinetic energy.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def geometricKineticEnergy
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) : ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.geometricKineticEnergy_eq
entries.docstring:
The geometric kinetic energy is one half the mass Riemannian metric applied to `v`
twice.
entries.snippet:
lemma geometricKineticEnergy_eq
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) :
    geometricKineticEnergy S q v =
      (1 / 2 : ℝ) * S.massRiemannianMetric.inner q v v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massRiemannianMetric_pos
entries.docstring: The oscillator mass Riemannian metric is positive definite.
entries.snippet:
lemma massRiemannianMetric_pos
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q)
    (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    0 < S.massRiemannianMetric.inner q v v

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.massRiemannianMetric_inner_apply
entries.docstring:
In the global coordinate, the oscillator mass metric is the mass-scaled Euclidean inner
product of coordinate representatives.
entries.snippet:
lemma massRiemannianMetric_inner_apply
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v w : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) :
    S.massRiemannianMetric.inner q v w =
      S.m * ⟪tangentCoord q v, tangentCoord q w⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.geometricKineticEnergy_massMetric_eq
entries.docstring:
The metric-induced kinetic energy for the mass metric has the standard
harmonic-oscillator coordinate form.
entries.snippet:
lemma geometricKineticEnergy_massMetric_eq
    (S : HarmonicOscillator) (q : ConfigurationSpace)
    (v : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) q) :
    geometricKineticEnergy S q v =
      (1 / 2 : ℝ) * S.m * ⟪tangentCoord q v, tangentCoord q v⟫_ℝ

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory
entries.docstring: A trajectory of the oscillator: a curve in the configuration manifold `Q`.
entries.snippet: abbrev Trajectory

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.coord
entries.docstring: The coordinate curve of a trajectory: its reading in the global Euclidean coordinate.
entries.snippet: def coord (γ : Trajectory) : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.toSpace
entries.docstring: The physical position of the oscillator along a trajectory, over time.
entries.snippet: def toSpace (γ : Trajectory) : Time → Space 1

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.coord_apply
entries.snippet: lemma coord_apply (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) : coord γ t = (γ t).val

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.contMDiff_iff_contDiff_coord
entries.docstring: A trajectory is smooth as a curve in `Q` iff its coordinate curve is ordinarily smooth.
entries.snippet:
lemma contMDiff_iff_contDiff_coord {n : WithTop ℕ∞} (γ : Trajectory) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, Time) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) n γ ↔
      ContDiff ℝ n (coord γ)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.velocity
entries.docstring: The geometric velocity of a trajectory at time `t`: a tangent vector at `γ t`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def velocity (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) :
    TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (γ t)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.mdifferentiableAt_iff_differentiableAt_coord
entries.docstring:
A trajectory is `MDifferentiableAt` a time iff its coordinate curve is ordinarily
differentiable there, since the two differ by the coordinate diffeomorphism.
entries.snippet:
lemma mdifferentiableAt_iff_differentiableAt_coord (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) :
    MDifferentiableAt 𝓘(ℝ, Time) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) γ t ↔
      DifferentiableAt ℝ (coord γ) t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.mfderiv_eq_mfderiv_coord
ClassicalMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.Trajectory.velocity_eq_deriv_coord
entries.docstring:
In the global coordinate, geometric velocity is represented by the time derivative of the
coordinate curve.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_eq_deriv_coord (γ : Trajectory) (t : Time) :
    velocity γ t = ∂ₜ (coord γ) t

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.isTotalTimeDerivative_neg
entries.docstring: Elementary fact: if δL is a time derivative, then so is -δL.
entries.snippet:
lemma isTotalTimeDerivative_neg {δL : Time → X → X → ℝ} (h :  IsTotalTimeDerivative δL) :
    IsTotalTimeDerivative (- δL)

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.totalTimeDerivative_contDiff
entries.docstring: If δL is a total time derivative (of a smooth function), then it is smooth
entries.snippet:
lemma totalTimeDerivative_contDiff {δL : Time → X → X → ℝ} (h : IsTotalTimeDerivative δL):
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ ↿δL

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.totalTimeDerivative_hasZeroVarGradient
entries.docstring: Total time derivative has a variational derivative, which is zero

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.totalTimeDerivative_hasVarGradientAt_equivalence
entries.docstring:
If two lagrangians, L and L', differ by a total time derivative, and L has a variational derivative
grad, then so does L'.
entries.snippet:
lemma totalTimeDerivative_hasVarGradientAt_equivalence [CompleteSpace X] (L δL : Time → X → X → ℝ)
    (hδL : IsTotalTimeDerivative δL)
    (q : Time → X)    (hq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ q) (grad : Time → X)
    (hgrad :  HasVarGradientAt (fun q' t => L t (q' t) (fderiv ℝ  q' t 1)) grad q) :
    HasVarGradientAt (fun q' t => (L + δL) t (q' t) (fderiv ℝ q' t 1)) grad q

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.totalTimeDerivative_varGradient_equivalenvce
entries.snippet:
lemma totalTimeDerivative_varGradient_equivalenvce [CompleteSpace X] (L L' : Time → X → X → ℝ)
    (htot : IsTotalTimeDerivative (L' - L))
    (q : Time → X) (hq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ q):
    (δ (q':=q), ∫ t, L' t (q' t) (fderiv ℝ q' t 1)) =
       (δ (q':=q), ∫ t, L t (q' t) (fderiv ℝ q' t 1))

entries.name: ClassicalMechanics.Lagrangian.totalTimeDerivative_eulerLagrange_equivalenvce
entries.docstring:
Corollary: If L and L' differ by a total time derivative, then the corresponding Euler-Lagrange
operators coincide
entries.snippet:
lemma totalTimeDerivative_eulerLagrange_equivalenvce [CompleteSpace X] (L L' : Time → X → X → ℝ)
    (htot : IsTotalTimeDerivative (L' - L)) (hContDiff : (ContDiff ℝ ∞ ↿L) ∨ (ContDiff ℝ ∞ ↿L'))
    (q : Time → X) (hq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ q) : eulerLagrangeOp L q = eulerLagrangeOp L' q

entries.name: RigidBody.angularMomentum
entries.docstring:
The angular momentum `L = ∫ r × (ω × r) dm` of a rigid body rotating with angular velocity `ω`
about its reference point (each body point at `r` moving with velocity `ω × r`). Its `i`-th
component is `ρ` applied to the scalar field `[r × (ω × r)]ᵢ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def angularMomentum (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ

entries.name: RigidBody.angularMomentum_eq_inertiaTensor_mulVec
entries.docstring:
The angular momentum of a rigid body equals its inertia tensor applied to the angular velocity:
`L = I ω`.
entries.snippet:
theorem angularMomentum_eq_inertiaTensor_mulVec (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    R.angularMomentum ω = R.inertiaTensor *ᵥ ω

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor
entries.docstring:
The angular velocity tensor `Ω(t) = Ṙ(t) R(t)ᵀ` of a rigid body in motion, where
`R(t) = orientation t`. It is the antisymmetric tensor `Ω` in the Landau–Lifshitz decomposition
`v = V + Ω × r` of the velocity of a point of the body.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def angularVelocityTensor (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor t = ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t * ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_transpose
entries.docstring:
The angular velocity tensor is skew-symmetric, `Ωᵀ = -Ω`: it lies in the Lie algebra `𝔰𝔬(d)`.
This is the litmus check that `Ω = Ṙ Rᵀ` is a genuine angular-velocity tensor, and follows by
differentiating the orthogonality identity `R Rᵀ = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_transpose (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    (M.angularVelocityTensor t)ᵀ = - M.angularVelocityTensor t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const
entries.docstring: A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero angular velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion d)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor = 0

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocity
entries.docstring:
The angular velocity *vector* `ω(t)` of a rigid body moving in three-dimensional space: the
vector dual to the angular velocity tensor `Ω(t)` under the hat map, `ω = Ωᵛ`. It is the angular
velocity `ω` in the Landau–Lifshitz decomposition `v = V + ω × r` of the velocity of a point of the
body, where `ω × r` is the cross product with `ω`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) : Fin 3 → ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocity_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocity_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocity t = crossProductVee (M.angularVelocityTensor t)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.crossProductMatrix_angularVelocity
entries.docstring:
The hat map recovers the angular velocity tensor from the angular velocity vector, `[ω]ₓ = Ω`.
This is the defining relationship between the vector and tensor forms of the angular velocity in
three dimensions; it holds because `Ω` is skew-symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma crossProductMatrix_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    crossProductMatrix (M.angularVelocity t) = M.angularVelocityTensor t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocity_of_orientation_const
entries.docstring: A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero angular velocity vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocity_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin 3) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.angularVelocity = 0

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_mul_orientation
entries.docstring:
The time derivative of the orientation is `Ṙ = Ω R`, recovering the orientation path from its
angular velocity tensor `Ω = Ṙ Rᵀ` via the orthogonality `Rᵀ R = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_mul_orientation (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor t * (M.orientation t).1 = ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_angularVelocity_cross
entries.docstring:
The rotational part of the velocity of the body point `y` is the cross product of the
angular velocity with the point's position relative to the centre of mass:
`Ṙ(t) (y − c) = ω(t) × (displacement t y − comTrajectory t)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_angularVelocity_cross (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (y : Space 3)
    (t : Time) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ (fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
      = M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq_angularVelocity
entries.docstring:
The Landau–Lifshitz velocity decomposition `v = V + ω × r` for a rigid body in three
dimensions: the velocity of a body point is the centre-of-mass velocity plus the cross product of
the angular velocity with the point's position relative to the centre of mass.
entries.snippet:
theorem velocity_eq_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (y : Space 3) (t : Time) (i : Fin 3)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1)) (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.velocity y t i = M.centerOfMassVelocity t i
        + (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j) i

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor
entries.docstring:
The body-frame (co-rotating) angular velocity tensor `Ω_body(t) = R(t)ᵀ Ṙ(t)` of a rigid body
in motion, where `R(t) = orientation t`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def bodyAngularVelocityTensor (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t = ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ * ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mul_bodyAngularVelocityTensor
entries.docstring:
The time derivative of the orientation is `Ṙ = R Ω_body`, recovering the orientation path from
its body-frame angular velocity tensor via the orthogonality `R Rᵀ = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma orientation_mul_bodyAngularVelocityTensor (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.orientation t).1 * M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t = ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.angularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj
entries.docstring:
The spatial tensor is the body-frame tensor rotated into the inertial frame,
`Ω = R Ω_body Rᵀ`.
entries.snippet:
lemma angularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.angularVelocityTensor t
      = (M.orientation t).1 * M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t * ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj
entries.docstring:
The body-frame tensor is the spatial tensor conjugated into the body frame,
`Ω_body = Rᵀ Ω R`.
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_eq_orientation_conj (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t
      = ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ * M.angularVelocityTensor t * (M.orientation t).1

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_transpose
entries.docstring:
The body-frame angular velocity tensor is skew-symmetric, `Ω_bodyᵀ = -Ω_body`: it lies in the
Lie algebra `𝔰𝔬(d)`, inherited from the spatial tensor by conjugation.
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_transpose (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    (M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t)ᵀ = - M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity
entries.docstring:
The body-frame angular velocity *vector* `ω_body(t)` of a rigid body moving in three-dimensional
space: the vector dual to the body-frame angular velocity tensor `Ω_body(t)` under the hat map,
`ω_body = Ω_bodyᵛ`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) : Fin 3 → ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocity_eq (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocity t = crossProductVee (M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.crossProductMatrix_bodyAngularVelocity
entries.docstring:
The hat map recovers the body-frame angular velocity tensor from the body-frame angular
velocity vector, `[ω_body]ₓ = Ω_body`; it holds because `Ω_body` is skew-symmetric.
entries.snippet:
lemma crossProductMatrix_bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    crossProductMatrix (M.bodyAngularVelocity t) = M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const
entries.docstring:
A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero body-frame angular velocity
tensor.
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocityTensor_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion d)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocityTensor = 0

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.bodyAngularVelocity_of_orientation_const
entries.docstring:
A rigid body whose orientation is constant in time has zero body-frame angular velocity
vector.
entries.snippet:
lemma bodyAngularVelocity_of_orientation_const (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin 3) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.bodyAngularVelocity = 0

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_orientation_bodyAngularVelocity_cross
entries.docstring:
The rotational velocity written through the body-frame angular velocity,
`Ṙ(t) v = R(t) (ω_body(t) × v)`: the derivative of the orientation acts as the body-frame angular
velocity `ω_body` crossed with `v`, rotated back into the inertial frame by `R`.
entries.snippet:
lemma deriv_orientation_mulVec_eq_orientation_bodyAngularVelocity_cross (M : RigidBodyMotion 3)
    (v : Fin 3 → ℝ) (t : Time)
    (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ v
      = (M.orientation t).1 *ᵥ (M.bodyAngularVelocity t ⨯₃ v)

entries.name: RigidBody.rho_one
entries.docstring: The mass distribution applied to the constant function `1` is the total mass.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma rho_one {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) :
    R.ρ (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯) = R.mass

entries.name: RigidBody.cmap
entries.docstring:
Bundle a smooth real-valued function on `Space d` as an element of the space of test
functions. Keeping this as a named constructor ensures the resulting type head stays
`ContMDiffMap`, so the module/ring operations and `comp` resolve correctly.
entries.snippet:
def cmap {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ f) :
    C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯

entries.name: RigidBody.cmap_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma cmap_apply {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ f) (y : Space d) :
    cmap f hf y = f y

entries.name: RigidBody.rho_coord_sub_centerOfMass
entries.docstring:
The first moment of the mass distribution about its own centre of mass vanishes:
for nonzero mass, `ρ` of the centred `j`-th coordinate function is zero.
entries.snippet:
lemma rho_coord_sub_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (R : RigidBody d) (h : R.mass ≠ 0) (j : Fin d) :
    R.ρ (cmap (fun y => y j - R.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)) = 0

entries.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy
entries.docstring:
The rotational kinetic energy of a rigid body rotating with angular velocity `ω` about its
reference point: half the contraction of `ω` with the inertia tensor, `T = ½ ω · (I ω)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def rotationalKineticEnergy (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_angularMomentum
entries.docstring:
The rotational kinetic energy is half the contraction of the angular velocity with the angular
momentum: `T = ½ ω · L`.
entries.snippet:
lemma rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_angularMomentum (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    R.rotationalKineticEnergy ω = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * (ω ⬝ᵥ R.angularMomentum ω)

entries.name: RigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_integral
entries.docstring:
The rotational kinetic energy equals the mass integral of the local rotational speed squared:
`T = ½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`.
entries.snippet:
theorem rotationalKineticEnergy_eq_integral (R : RigidBody 3) (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    R.rotationalKineticEnergy ω
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * R.ρ ⟨fun x => (ω ⨯₃ (x : Fin 3 → ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ (ω ⨯₃ (x : Fin 3 → ℝ)),
        ContDiff.contMDiff <| (contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross ω).comp
          (contDiff_pi.mpr fun i => Space.eval_contDiff i)⟩

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy
entries.docstring:
The total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion at time `t`: half the mass integral of the
squared speed of the body points, `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm`, with the point velocity taken in the
closed form `velocityClosedForm`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def kineticEnergy {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_integral_velocity
entries.docstring:
For a differentiable motion the integrand of `kineticEnergy` is the squared speed of the
honest point velocity: `T = ½ ∫ ⟪v, v⟫ dm` with `v = ∂ₜ (displacement · y)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_eq_integral_velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.kineticEnergy t = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap
      (fun y => (⟪M.velocity y t, M.velocity y t⟫_ℝ))
      (by
        simp only [← M.velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity t hR hX]
        exact M.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner t))

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_integrand_split
entries.docstring:
The squared-speed integrand of `kineticEnergy` splits into the squared rotational speed
`|Ṙ (y − c)|²`, a term linear in the body-frame coordinate `y − c`, and the constant squared
centre-of-mass speed `⟪V, V⟫`.
entries.snippet:
lemma kineticEnergy_integrand_split {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    cmap (fun y => (⟪M.velocityClosedForm t y, M.velocityClosedForm t y⟫_ℝ))
        (M.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner t)
      = cmap (fun y =>
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) ⬝ᵥ
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j))
          (by simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]; fun_prop)
        + ∑ j, (2 * (((M.centerOfMassVelocity t : Fin d → ℝ) ᵥ*
              ∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) j)) •
            cmap (fun y => y j - M.centerOfMass j) (by fun_prop)
        + (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ) •
            (1 : C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_rotational
entries.docstring:
**König's theorem**, general form: the total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion splits
into the kinetic energy of the centre of mass plus the rotational energy about the centre of
mass, `T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + ½ ∫ |Ṙ (y − c)|² dm`.
entries.snippet:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_rotational {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap (fun y =>
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) ⬝ᵥ
            (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j))
          (by simp only [dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]; fun_prop))

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_angularVelocity
entries.docstring:
**König's theorem** in three dimensions: the total kinetic energy of a rigid body in motion
splits as `T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + ½ ∫ |ω × r|² dm`, with `ω` the angular velocity vector and
`r = displacement − comTrajectory` the position of the body point relative to the centre of
mass.
entries.snippet:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_angularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.ρ (cmap (fun y =>
            (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j) ⬝ᵥ
            (M.angularVelocity t ⨯₃ fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j))
          (by
            exact (contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross (M.angularVelocity t)).comp
              (contDiff_pi.mpr fun j =>
                ((Space.eval_contDiff j).comp (M.displacement_contDiff t)).sub
                  contDiff_const)))

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_bodyAngularVelocity
entries.docstring:
**König's theorem** in the body frame. The total kinetic energy `M.kineticEnergy t`, formed from
the lab-frame point velocities, splits at the centre of mass (`centerOfMass = 0`) as
`T = ½ M ⟪V, V⟫ + rotationalKineticEnergy ω_body`. The rotational energy is a frame-independent
scalar, so it is evaluated here from the *body-frame* angular velocity `ω_body`: the spatial form
`|Ṙ (y − c)|²` and the body form `|ω_body × (y − c)|²` agree because
`Ṙ (y − c) = R (ω_body × (y − c))` and `R`, being orthogonal, preserves the norm.
entries.snippet:
theorem kineticEnergy_eq_translational_add_bodyAngularVelocity (M : RigidBodyMotion 3) (t : Time)
    (h : M.mass ≠ 0) (hR : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t)
    (hc : M.centerOfMass = 0) :
    M.kineticEnergy t
      = (1 / (2 : ℝ)) * M.mass * (⟪M.centerOfMassVelocity t, M.centerOfMassVelocity t⟫_ℝ)
        + M.toRigidBody.rotationalKineticEnergy (M.bodyAngularVelocity t)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion
entries.docstring:
A motion of a rigid body in `d`-dimensional space: the body together with the inertial-frame
trajectory of its centre of mass and its time-dependent orientation (a rotation about the centre
of mass).
entries.snippet:
structure RigidBodyMotion (d : ℕ) extends RigidBody d where
  comTrajectory : Time → Space d
  orientation : Time → Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mul_transpose
entries.docstring: The orientation matrix is special orthogonal, so `R Rᵀ = 1`.
entries.snippet:
lemma orientation_mul_transpose {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.orientation t).1 * ((M.orientation t).1)ᵀ = 1

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity
entries.docstring:
The velocity of the centre of mass of a rigid body in motion, defined as the time-derivative
of its centre-of-mass trajectory. This is the velocity `V` in the Landau–Lifshitz decomposition
`v = V + Ω × r` of the velocity of a point of the body.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def centerOfMassVelocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) : Time → Space d

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma centerOfMassVelocity_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.centerOfMassVelocity = ∂ₜ M.comTrajectory

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.centerOfMassVelocity_of_comTrajectory_const
entries.docstring: A rigid body whose centre of mass is stationary has zero centre-of-mass velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma centerOfMassVelocity_of_comTrajectory_const {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (c : Space d)
    (h : M.comTrajectory = fun _ => c) : M.centerOfMassVelocity = 0

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.linearMomentum
entries.docstring:
The linear momentum of a rigid body in motion: the total mass times the velocity of the
centre of mass.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def linearMomentum {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) : Time → Space d

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.linearMomentum_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma linearMomentum_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.linearMomentum = fun t => M.mass • M.centerOfMassVelocity t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement
entries.docstring:
The rigid displacement carrying the body frame into the inertial frame at time `t`: the
rotation `orientation t` about the centre of mass, followed by the translation placing the centre
of mass at `comTrajectory t`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def displacement {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : Space d → Space d

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement_apply
entries.docstring: The `k`-th coordinate of the rigid displacement applied to `y`.
entries.snippet:
lemma displacement_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) (k : Fin d) :
    M.displacement t y k =
      (∑ j, (M.orientation t).val k j * (y j - M.centerOfMass j)) + M.comTrajectory t k

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.displacement_contDiff
entries.snippet:
lemma displacement_contDiff {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (M.displacement t)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.orientation_mulVec_sub_centerOfMass
entries.docstring:
Rotating the body-frame position of `y` relative to the centre of mass gives its
inertial-frame position relative to the moving centre of mass:
`R(t) (y − c) = displacement t y − comTrajectory t`.
entries.snippet:
lemma orientation_mulVec_sub_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (y : Space d) :
    (M.orientation t).1 *ᵥ (fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
      = fun j => M.displacement t y j - M.comTrajectory t j

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution
entries.docstring:
The mass distribution of the rigid body in motion at time `t`: the pushforward of the
body-fixed mass distribution along the rigid displacement, acting on a test function `f` by
`f ↦ ρ (f ∘ displacement t)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def massDistribution {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) : RigidBody d where

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution_mass
entries.docstring:
The motion preserves the total mass: the mass distribution at any time `t` has the same total
mass as the body.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma massDistribution_mass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    (M.massDistribution t).mass = M.mass

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.contMDiffMap_sum_apply
entries.docstring: Evaluation commutes with finite sums of smooth functions.

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.massDistribution_centerOfMass
entries.docstring:
The centre of mass of the moving mass distribution tracks the prescribed trajectory: for a
body of nonzero mass, the centre of mass of `massDistribution M t` is exactly `comTrajectory t`.
This is the decisive check that `comTrajectory` and `orientation` are wired correctly in
`RigidBodyMotion`.
entries.snippet:
lemma massDistribution_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (h : M.mass ≠ 0) :
    (M.massDistribution t).centerOfMass = M.comTrajectory t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity
entries.docstring:
The velocity of the material point `y` of a rigid body in motion: the inertial-frame time
derivative of the trajectory `s ↦ displacement s y` of that point.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) : Time → Space d

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_eq {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time) :
    M.velocity y t = ∂ₜ (fun s => M.displacement s y) t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_apply
entries.docstring:
The `i`-th component of the velocity of a body point is the time derivative of the `i`-th
coordinate of its inertial-frame trajectory.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time) (i : Fin d)
    (hd : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => M.displacement s y)) :
    M.velocity y t i = ∂ₜ (fun s => M.displacement s y i) t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_centerOfMass
entries.docstring:
The material point at the centre of mass moves with the centre-of-mass velocity, for any
motion: `v(centreOfMass) = V`. This is the velocity counterpart of `massDistribution_centerOfMass`.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_centerOfMass {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) :
    M.velocity M.centerOfMass = M.centerOfMassVelocity

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_of_orientation_const
entries.docstring:
A rigid body in pure translation (constant orientation) has every point moving with the
centre-of-mass velocity: `v = V`.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_of_orientation_const {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d)
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (h : M.orientation = fun _ => R) :
    M.velocity y = M.centerOfMassVelocity

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocity_eq_deriv_orientation
entries.docstring:
The velocity of a body point decomposes as `v = Ṙ (y − c) + V`: the rate of change of the
orientation acting on the body-frame position, plus the centre-of-mass velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocity_eq_deriv_orientation {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (y : Space d) (t : Time)
    (i : Fin d) (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) :
    M.velocity y t i
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) i
        + M.centerOfMassVelocity t i

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm
entries.docstring:
The closed form `Ṙ(t) (y − c) + V(t)` of the velocity of the body point `y` at time `t`.
Unlike `velocity` — whose junk values on non-differentiable motions need not vary continuously
with `y` — it is polynomial in `y` for any motion, so its squared speed can be bundled as the
smooth integrand of the total kinetic energy; for differentiable motions the two agree, see
`velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def velocityClosedForm {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) :
    Space d

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_apply
entries.docstring: The `i`-th coordinate of the closed-form velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocityClosedForm_apply {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d)
    (i : Fin d) :
    M.velocityClosedForm t y i
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j) i
        + M.centerOfMassVelocity t i

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_val
entries.docstring: The closed-form velocity as a plain vector-valued function of the coordinates of `y`.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocityClosedForm_val {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) (y : Space d) :
    (M.velocityClosedForm t y : Fin d → ℝ)
      = (∂ₜ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1) t *ᵥ fun j => y j - M.centerOfMass j)
        + (M.centerOfMassVelocity t : Fin d → ℝ)

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity
entries.docstring: For a differentiable motion the closed-form velocity is the honest point velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma velocityClosedForm_eq_velocity {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time)
    (hR : Differentiable ℝ (fun s => (M.orientation s).1))
    (hX : Differentiable ℝ M.comTrajectory) (y : Space d) :
    M.velocityClosedForm t y = M.velocity y t

entries.name: RigidBodyMotion.contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner
entries.docstring: The squared speed of a body point, in closed form, is a smooth function of the point.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_velocityClosedForm_inner {d : ℕ} (M : RigidBodyMotion d) (t : Time) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ fun y : Space d => (⟪M.velocityClosedForm t y, M.velocityClosedForm t y⟫_ℝ)

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial
entries.docstring:
A thermoelectric material in the linear-response regime, characterized by
its four transport coefficients.
entries.snippet:
structure ThermoelectricMaterial where
  S : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  κl : ℝ
  κe : ℝ
  σ_pos : 0 < σ
  κl_pos : 0 < κl
  κe_nonneg : 0 ≤ κe

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.powerFactor
entries.docstring: The thermoelectric power factor `PF = σ S²` of a material.
entries.snippet: def powerFactor (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) : ℝ

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.powerFactor_pos
entries.docstring: The power factor is positive when the Seebeck coefficient is nonzero.
entries.snippet:
lemma powerFactor_pos {M : ThermoelectricMaterial} (hS : M.S ≠ 0) :
    0 < M.powerFactor

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.totalThermalConductivity
entries.docstring:
The total thermal conductivity `κl + κe` of a material, the sum of the
lattice (phonon) and electronic contributions.
entries.snippet: def totalThermalConductivity (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) : ℝ

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.totalThermalConductivity_pos
entries.docstring: The total thermal conductivity is positive.
entries.snippet:
lemma totalThermalConductivity_pos (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) :
    0 < M.totalThermalConductivity

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit
entries.docstring:
The dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit
`zT = PF · T / (κl + κe)` of a material at absolute temperature `T`.
entries.snippet: def figureOfMerit (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) (T : ℝ) : ℝ

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_eq
entries.docstring:
The figure of merit in its standard flat form
`zT = σ S² T / (κl + κe)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma figureOfMerit_eq (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) (T : ℝ) :
    M.figureOfMerit T = M.σ * M.S ^ 2 * T / (M.κl + M.κe)

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_pos
entries.docstring:
The figure of merit is positive at positive temperature when the Seebeck
coefficient is nonzero.

entries.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_le_of_le
entries.docstring:
Lowering the lattice thermal conductivity raises the figure of merit: if
`M.κl ≤ κl'` then the material with lattice conductivity `κl'` (all other
coefficients equal) has the smaller `zT`. This is the phonon-glass
electron-crystal design principle: scatter phonons without degrading
electronic transport. Note the hypotheses: no condition on the Seebeck
coefficient is needed, since monotonicity only requires the numerator
`σ S² T` to be nonnegative.

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow
entries.docstring:
A fluid flow equipped with Cauchy stress and specific body-force fields.

These are the additional independent fields needed to state a local momentum balance. The Cauchy
stress represents contact forces, and the specific body force represents volumetric force per unit
mass. Pressure and viscosity enter through stress laws rather than as redundant fields of
`CauchyFlow` itself.
entries.snippet:
structure CauchyFlow (d : ℕ) extends FluidFlow d where
  stress : StressTensor d
  specificBodyForce : VectorField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.HasBodyForcePotential
entries.docstring:
A flow has body-force potential `Phi` when its specific body force is minus the gradient of
`Phi`.
entries.snippet: def HasBodyForcePotential (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (potential : Space d → ℝ) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.HasConservativeBodyForce
entries.docstring: A flow has conservative body force when its specific body force has some potential.
entries.snippet: def HasConservativeBodyForce (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.IsInviscid
entries.docstring:
A Cauchy flow is inviscid with pressure `p` when its stress is the isotropic pressure stress
`-p I`.

In this formulation, inviscid means that the Cauchy stress has no viscous or shear contribution.
It does not rule out body forces; those are carried separately by `CauchyFlow.specificBodyForce`.
entries.snippet: def IsInviscid (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (pressure : ScalarField d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.matrixDiv_inviscid_pressure_stress
entries.docstring: The matrix divergence of the inviscid pressure stress `-p I` is `-grad p`.
entries.snippet:
lemma matrixDiv_inviscid_pressure_stress (d : ℕ) (pressureAtTime : Space d → ℝ) :
    matrixDiv d (fun x => (-(pressureAtTime x)) • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)) =
      -∇ pressureAtTime

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.matrixDiv_stress_eq_neg_grad_pressure_of_is_inviscid
entries.docstring:
In an inviscid Cauchy flow, the stress-divergence force is the usual
negative pressure-gradient term.
entries.snippet:
theorem matrixDiv_stress_eq_neg_grad_pressure_of_is_inviscid
    (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (pressure : ScalarField d)
    (hInviscid : IsInviscid d flow pressure) :
    ∀ t, matrixDiv d (flow.stress t) = -∇ (pressure t)

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.CauchyMomentumEquation
entries.docstring:
Conservation of momentum in conservative matrix-divergence form.

The equation is

`partial_t (rho u) + matrixDiv (rho u ⊗ u) = matrixDiv sigma + rho f`.

Here `stress` is intentionally not yet specialized to a constitutive law.
entries.snippet: def CauchyMomentumEquation (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.ConvectiveCauchyMomentumEquation
entries.docstring:
Conservation of momentum in convective form.

The equation is

`rho (partial_t u + (u · ∇)u) = matrixDiv sigma + rho f`.

Here `stress` is intentionally not yet specialized to a constitutive law.
entries.snippet: def ConvectiveCauchyMomentumEquation (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.cauchyMomentumEquation_iff_convectiveCauchyMomentumEquation
entries.docstring:
The conservative and convective Cauchy momentum equations are equivalent when the classical
continuity equation holds.

The differentiability assumptions are exactly the product-rule assumptions used to rewrite
`partial_t (rho u)` and `matrixDiv (rho u ⊗ u)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma cauchyMomentumEquation_iff_convectiveCauchyMomentumEquation
    (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d)
    (hContinuity : FluidFlow.ClassicalContinuityEquation d flow.toFluidFlow)
    (hRhoTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : ∀ t, Differentiable ℝ (FluidFlow.momentumDensity d flow.toFluidFlow t))
    (hVelocitySpace : ∀ t, Differentiable ℝ (flow.velocity t)) :
    CauchyMomentumEquation d flow ↔ ConvectiveCauchyMomentumEquation d flow

entries.name: FluidDynamics.navier_stokes_iff_convective_navier_stokes
entries.docstring:
The conservative and convective Navier-Stokes forms are equivalent when the fields are
differentiable enough for the product rules.
entries.snippet:
theorem navier_stokes_iff_convective_navier_stokes
    (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d)
    (pressure shearViscosity secondViscosity : ScalarField d)
    (hRhoTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : ∀ t,
      Differentiable ℝ (FluidFlow.momentumDensity d flow.toFluidFlow t))
    (hVelocitySpace : ∀ t, Differentiable ℝ (flow.velocity t)) :
    NavierStokes d flow pressure shearViscosity secondViscosity ↔
      ConvectiveNavierStokes d flow pressure shearViscosity secondViscosity

entries.name: FluidDynamics.CauchyFlow.IsNewtonian
entries.docstring: A Cauchy flow is Newtonian when its stress tensor has the Newtonian constitutive form.
entries.snippet:
def IsNewtonian
    (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d)
    (pressure shearViscosity secondViscosity : ScalarField d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.Euler
entries.docstring: The conservative Euler equations: continuity, Cauchy momentum, and inviscid stress.
entries.snippet: def Euler (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (pressure : ScalarField d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.ConvectiveEuler
entries.docstring:
The convective Euler equations: continuity, convective Cauchy momentum, and inviscid
stress.
entries.snippet: def ConvectiveEuler (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (pressure : ScalarField d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.euler_iff_convectiveEuler
entries.docstring:
The conservative and convective Euler forms are equivalent when the fields are
differentiable enough for the product rules.
entries.snippet:
theorem euler_iff_convectiveEuler
    (d : ℕ) (flow : CauchyFlow d) (pressure : ScalarField d)
    (hRhoTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : ∀ t x, DifferentiableAt ℝ (flow.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : ∀ t,
      Differentiable ℝ (FluidFlow.momentumDensity d flow.toFluidFlow t))
    (hVelocitySpace : ∀ t, Differentiable ℝ (flow.velocity t)) :
    Euler d flow pressure ↔ ConvectiveEuler d flow pressure

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow
entries.docstring:
The density and velocity fields of a fluid on `d`-dimensional space.

These fields are the independent data needed for kinematics and mass transport. Quantities such as
mass flux, momentum density, and material acceleration are derived from them. Dynamic and
thermodynamic fields are introduced only by extension structures whose statements need them.
entries.snippet:
structure FluidFlow (d : ℕ) where
  rho : MassDensity d
  velocity : VelocityField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.ClassicalContinuityEquation
entries.docstring:
Classical conservation of mass in conservative form, `partial_t rho + div (rho u) = 0`.

The equation is asserted at points where the time derivative of `rho` and the spatial
divergence of `rho u` are classical derivatives.
entries.snippet: def ClassicalContinuityEquation (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.continuityResidual
entries.docstring:
The scalar continuity-equation residual
`partial_t rho + div (rho u)`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def continuityResidual (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Time → Space d → ℝ

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.SmoothContinuityEquation
entries.docstring:
A stronger continuity equation for globally differentiable fields.

This version records the first-order regularity needed by the classical continuity equation:
the density is differentiable in time, the mass flux `rho u` is differentiable in space, and
the continuity residual vanishes everywhere.
entries.snippet: def SmoothContinuityEquation (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.classicalContinuityEquation_of_smoothContinuityEquation
entries.docstring: A smooth continuity equation satisfies the guarded classical continuity equation.
entries.snippet:
lemma classicalContinuityEquation_of_smoothContinuityEquation
    (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) :
    SmoothContinuityEquation d fluid → ClassicalContinuityEquation d fluid

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.incompressibilityResidual
entries.docstring: The incompressibility residual, given by the divergence of the velocity field.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def incompressibilityResidual (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) :
    Time → Space d → ℝ

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.ClassicalIncompressible
entries.docstring:
A classical incompressible flow has divergence-free velocity at points where the velocity
field is differentiable.
entries.snippet: def ClassicalIncompressible (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.SmoothIncompressible
entries.docstring:
A smooth incompressible flow has globally differentiable velocity and vanishing
incompressibility residual everywhere.
entries.snippet: def SmoothIncompressible (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.classicalIncompressible_of_smoothIncompressible
entries.docstring: A smooth incompressible flow is classically incompressible.
entries.snippet:
lemma classicalIncompressible_of_smoothIncompressible
    (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) :
    SmoothIncompressible d fluid → ClassicalIncompressible d fluid

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.materialDerivative
entries.docstring: The material derivative `D_t f = partial_t f + u · grad f` of a scalar field.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def materialDerivative (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d)
    (field : ScalarField d) : ScalarField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.specificKineticEnergy
entries.docstring: The specific kinetic energy `|u|^2 / 2` of a fluid flow.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def specificKineticEnergy (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : ScalarField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.momentumDensity
entries.docstring: The momentum density `rho u`.
entries.snippet: def momentumDensity (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : MomentumDensityField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.momentumFlux
entries.docstring: The convective momentum flux `rho u ⊗ u`.
entries.snippet: def momentumFlux (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : Time → Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.convectiveTerm
entries.docstring: The nonlinear transport term `(u · ∇)u`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def convectiveTerm (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : VectorField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.materialAcceleration
entries.docstring: The material acceleration `∂ₜ u + (u · ∇)u`.
entries.snippet: noncomputable def materialAcceleration (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d) : VectorField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.timeDeriv_smul_velocity
entries.docstring: Product rule for the time derivative of a scalar field times a velocity field.
entries.snippet:
lemma timeDeriv_smul_velocity (d : ℕ) (rhoAtPosition : Time → ℝ)
    (velocityAtPosition : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : Time)
    (hRho : DifferentiableAt ℝ rhoAtPosition t)
    (hVelocity : DifferentiableAt ℝ velocityAtPosition t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t' => rhoAtPosition t' • velocityAtPosition t') t =
      rhoAtPosition t • ∂ₜ velocityAtPosition t + ∂ₜ rhoAtPosition t • velocityAtPosition t

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.timeDeriv_momentumDensity
entries.docstring: Product rule for the time derivative of the momentum density `rho u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma timeDeriv_momentumDensity (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hRho : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocity : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.velocity · x) t) :
    ∂ₜ (momentumDensity d fluid · x) t =
      fluid.rho t x • ∂ₜ (fluid.velocity · x) t + ∂ₜ (fluid.rho · x) t • fluid.velocity t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.spaceDeriv_momentumFlux_component
entries.docstring: Product rule for one spatial derivative of one component of `rho u ⊗ u`.
entries.snippet:
lemma spaceDeriv_momentumFlux_component (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i j : Fin d)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocity : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    ∂[j] (fun x' => momentumFlux d fluid t x' i j) x =
      fluid.velocity t x i • ∂[j] (fun x' => momentumDensity d fluid t x' j) x +
      ∂[j] (fun x' => fluid.velocity t x' i) x • momentumDensity d fluid t x j

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.matrixDiv_momentumFlux
entries.docstring: The matrix divergence of `rho u ⊗ u` split into continuity and convective parts.
entries.snippet:
lemma matrixDiv_momentumFlux (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocity : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    matrixDiv d (momentumFlux d fluid t) x =
      (∇ ⬝ momentumDensity d fluid t) x • fluid.velocity t x +
        fluid.rho t x • convectiveTerm d fluid t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.momentumTransport_eq_materialAcceleration_add_continuityResidual
entries.docstring:
The conservative momentum transport terms equal mass density times material acceleration plus
the continuity residual times velocity.
entries.snippet:
lemma momentumTransport_eq_materialAcceleration_add_continuityResidual
    (d : ℕ) (fluid : FluidFlow d)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hRhoTime : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.rho · x) t)
    (hVelocityTime : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fluid.velocity · x) t)
    (hMomentumDensity : Differentiable ℝ (momentumDensity d fluid t))
    (hVelocitySpace : Differentiable ℝ (fluid.velocity t)) :
    ∂ₜ (momentumDensity d fluid · x) t + matrixDiv d (momentumFlux d fluid t) x =
      fluid.rho t x • materialAcceleration d fluid t x +
        continuityResidual d fluid t x • fluid.velocity t x

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.velocityGradient
entries.docstring: The spatial velocity-gradient matrix, with entries `partial_j u_i`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def velocityGradient (d : ℕ) (flow : FluidFlow d) :
    Time → Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

entries.name: FluidDynamics.FluidFlow.newtonianStressTensor
entries.docstring:
The Newtonian stress tensor
`-p I + mu (grad u + grad u^T) + lambda (div u) I`.

The scalar fields are pressure, shear viscosity, and second viscosity.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def newtonianStressTensor (d : ℕ) (flow : FluidFlow d)
    (pressure shearViscosity secondViscosity : ScalarField d) : StressTensor d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.ThermodynamicCauchyFlow
entries.docstring:
A Cauchy flow equipped with thermodynamic entropy and enthalpy fields.

These fields are independent of the kinematic and momentum-balance data unless additional
thermodynamic constitutive laws are imposed. They are sufficient for the current isentropic and
Bernoulli APIs; other thermodynamic fields belong in later extensions that require them.
entries.snippet:
structure ThermodynamicCauchyFlow (d : ℕ) extends CauchyFlow d where
  entropy : ScalarField d
  enthalpy : ScalarField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.bernoulliFunction
entries.docstring: The Bernoulli function `|u|^2 / 2 + h + Phi`.
entries.snippet:
noncomputable def bernoulliFunction
    (d : ℕ) (flow : ThermodynamicCauchyFlow d) (potential : Space d → ℝ) : ScalarField d

entries.name: FluidDynamics.LocalBernoulliLaw
entries.docstring: A local Bernoulli law: the Bernoulli function has zero spatial gradient.
entries.snippet:
def LocalBernoulliLaw
    (d : ℕ) (flow : ThermodynamicCauchyFlow d) (potential : Space d → ℝ) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.BernoulliLaw
entries.docstring: A global Bernoulli law: the Bernoulli function is spatially constant at each time.
entries.snippet:
def BernoulliLaw
    (d : ℕ) (flow : ThermodynamicCauchyFlow d) (potential : Space d → ℝ) : Prop

entries.name: FluidDynamics.ThermodynamicCauchyFlow.IsIsentropic
entries.docstring:
A thermodynamic flow is isentropic when the entropy is materially conserved along the
underlying fluid velocity field.
entries.snippet: def IsIsentropic (d : ℕ) (flow : ThermodynamicCauchyFlow d) : Prop

entries.name: Matrix.cross_cross_self_apply
entries.docstring:
The component form of the triple cross product `v ⨯₃ (w ⨯₃ v)`: by the `bac−cab` identity its
`i`-th entry is `|v|² wᵢ − (v · w) vᵢ`, written with the explicit component sums `∑ k, (v k)²` and
`∑ j, v j * w j`.
entries.snippet:
lemma cross_cross_self_apply (v w : Fin 3 → ℝ) (i : Fin 3) :
    (v ⨯₃ (w ⨯₃ v)) i = (∑ k, (v k) ^ 2) * w i - (∑ j, v j * w j) * v i

entries.name: Matrix.dotProduct_cross_cross_self
entries.docstring:
Contracting `w` with the triple cross product `v ⨯₃ (w ⨯₃ v)` gives `(w ⨯₃ v) ⬝ᵥ (w ⨯₃ v)`
(over `ℝ`, the squared length `|w × v|²`), by two cyclic permutations of the scalar triple
product.
entries.snippet:
lemma dotProduct_cross_cross_self {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (v w : Fin 3 → R) :
    w ⬝ᵥ (v ⨯₃ (w ⨯₃ v)) = (w ⨯₃ v) ⬝ᵥ (w ⨯₃ v)

entries.name: Matrix.contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross
entries.docstring:
The squared length `(ω ⨯₃ v) ⬝ᵥ (ω ⨯₃ v)` of the cross product with a fixed vector `ω` is a
smooth function of `v`.
entries.snippet:
lemma contDiff_cross_dotProduct_cross (ω : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ fun v : Fin 3 → ℝ => (ω ⨯₃ v) ⬝ᵥ (ω ⨯₃ v)

entries.name: Matrix.crossProductMatrix_crossProductVee
entries.docstring:
On skew-symmetric matrices the hat map is also a right inverse of the vee map: if `Aᵀ = -A`
then `[Aᵛ]ₓ = A`. Together with `crossProductVee_crossProductMatrix` this identifies `ℝ³` with the
skew-symmetric `3 × 3` matrices `𝖘𝖔(3)`.
entries.snippet:
lemma crossProductMatrix_crossProductVee {A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ} (hA : Aᵀ = -A) :
    crossProductMatrix (crossProductVee A) = A

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution
entries.docstring: The Mathlib tempered distribution associated to a Physlib distribution.
entries.snippet: def toTemperedDistribution (u : E →d[ℂ] F) : 𝓢'(E, F)

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution_apply
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toTemperedDistribution_apply (u : E →d[ℂ] F) (η : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    u.toTemperedDistribution η = u η

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution_fourierTransform
entries.docstring: Conversion to Mathlib tempered distributions commutes with the Fourier transform.
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma toTemperedDistribution_fourierTransform (u : E →d[ℂ] F) :
    (u.fourierTransform E F).toTemperedDistribution = 𝓕 u.toTemperedDistribution

entries.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure
entries.docstring:
The scalar distribution associated to a finite measure, acting on a Schwartz map by
integration.
